subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: collects real-time data from the physical city.

subsystems.name: Geospatial model
subsystems.role: provides the 3D geometric and semantic representation of buildings, roads, terrain and vegetation.

subsystems.name: Data integration platform
subsystems.role: ingests, cleans and harmonises heterogeneous data streams into a common operating picture.

subsystems.name: Simulation engine
subsystems.role: runs physics-based and agent-based models of city systems.

subsystems.name: AI and predictive analytics
subsystems.role: forecasts future states and suggests interventions.

subsystems.name: Visualisation and interface
subsystems.role: lets planners and operators explore the twin and act on its outputs.

buildSteps.title: Define objectives and scope
buildSteps.detail: Decide which city systems the twin will cover — for example traffic, energy, flooding or emergency response — and what decisions it must support.

buildSteps.title: Capture baseline geospatial data
buildSteps.detail: Fly LiDAR and photogrammetry surveys, collect satellite imagery, and gather existing BIM and cadastral records to build a complete 3D base map.

buildSteps.title: Construct the 3D city model
buildSteps.detail: Process point clouds into meshes, classify features such as buildings, roads, trees and terrain, and attach semantic attributes like building height and use.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and connect sensors
buildSteps.detail: Install new IoT devices where needed and link existing feeds — traffic loops, weather stations, utility meters — into a common network.

buildSteps.title: Build the data integration layer
buildSteps.detail: Create streaming pipelines to ingest, clean and store real-time and historical data, with APIs so external systems can publish and subscribe.

buildSteps.title: Develop and calibrate simulation models
buildSteps.detail: Build traffic, energy, flood or crowd models, then tune them against recorded data so their predictions match observed behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the twin
buildSteps.detail: Connect the 3D model, live data and simulations into a single platform, and validate it by replaying past events and comparing outcomes.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Use the twin for planning, real-time monitoring and emergency drills; continuously update the model as the city changes and sensors are added or replaced.

prerequisites.why: real-time feeds from thousands of sensors need reliable fibre and 5G links.
storing and processing city-scale data in real time exceeds local hardware.
LiDAR and BIM are mature, but full-city coverage at useful detail is still incomplete in many places.
deployments are growing but remain patchy and siloed across city departments.
formats such as CityGML and IFC help, but seamless exchange across vendors and domains is not yet routine.
machine learning works for specific tasks, but robust real-time forecasting across coupled city systems is still developing.

pathway.milestone: static 3D models and dashboards for planning and public consultation
pathway.unlocks: better visualisation of proposed developments and clearer communication with citizens.

pathway.milestone: real-time operational twins for traffic, energy and emergency response in major cities
pathway.unlocks: live congestion management, demand response and faster incident coordination.

pathway.milestone: cross-domain twins that couple water, waste, transport and energy
pathway.unlocks: integrated resource planning and resilience against cascading failures.

pathway.milestone: predictive, semi-autonomous city management with closed-loop control
pathway.unlocks: continuous optimisation of services, though with significant governance and cybersecurity challenges.
